status: partial draft; all runtime cases unexecuted

requirements.title: analysis and transparent audio
requirements.contract: Spectrum performs real-time analysis of incoming audio; its graph has vertical dB and horizontal frequency/pitch axes. It is a measurement tool and does not alter incoming audio. Graph refresh timing and audio-through precision/latency are U.

requirements.title: Block measurement size
requirements.contract: Block chooses the number of samples analyzed per measurement. Larger settings improve accuracy and increase CPU demand according to the manual. The supported sample-count list, FFT size mapping, overlap, zero padding and accuracy/CPU bounds are U.

requirements.title: analysis channel
requirements.contract: Channel selects analysis of left, right or both. The channel-combination algorithm, stereo summation/normalization and cancellation behavior of Both are U. This setting is not documented as changing audio output.

requirements.title: Refresh
requirements.contract: Refresh controls how often analysis occurs. Faster response trades greater CPU use for accuracy in the manual’s description. Exact domain, units, scheduling, update quantization, hidden-view behavior and wall-clock versus transport coupling are U.

requirements.title: Avg
requirements.contract: Avg selects how many sample blocks are averaged for each display update. At one, each block is shown; larger values smooth the display over time. The domain, accumulation method, reset/priming, decibel-versus-linear averaging and weighting/window are U.

requirements.title: Graph
requirements.contract: Graph switches between a single interpolated line and discrete frequency bins. Interpolation, bin positions, pixel rendering and amplitude calibration are U.

requirements.title: maximum trace and reset
requirements.contract: Peak levels are retained until the song restarts. Max toggles display of accumulated maximum amplitude; when Max is enabled, clicking the display resets the maximum. Whether Max off clears accumulation, reset scope, restart event definition and reset timing are U.

requirements.title: horizontal scaling
requirements.contract: Scale X offers linear, logarithmic and semitone. Logarithmic and semitone use the same scaling, with top legends in Hz or note names respectively. Exact axis domain, note tuning reference, legend rounding and sample-rate-dependent limits are U.

requirements.title: pointer readout
requirements.contract: Hovering the display shows a box with amplitude, frequency and note name at pointer location. This is a location readout, not a documented peak-picking or pitch-detector result. Units/rounding, off-graph behavior and frequency-to-note tie rules are U.

requirements.title: manual range navigation
requirements.contract: Range/Auto selects manual or automatic dynamic range. In Range mode, amplitude-legending drags scroll vertically and zoom horizontally; Range sliders set minimum/maximum amplitude shown. Slider domain, allowed ordering, zoom limits and gestures outside the legending are U.

requirements.title: Auto range
requirements.contract: Auto scales the display to incoming level; Range sliders and zooming are disabled. Algorithm, margins, hysteresis, decay and retained manual range are U.

requirements.title: display location
requirements.contract: The title-bar button or double-click in the display toggles graph placement between device chain and Live’s main window. Geometry, focus/selection, keyboard accessibility and view/preset retention are U.

requirements.title: target stored analysis state
requirements.contract: Latest schema and eleven shipped Spectrum presets contain range/axis, analysis, Length, Window, channel, averaging and refresh fields. Window=3 is an observed stored code in these presets, not a named window function, selectable UI control, FFT kernel or mathematical law. Preset labels do not prove block counts or enum meanings.

requirements.title: numerical and lifecycle gaps
requirements.contract: Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause is U. FFT/window/kernel, dB normalization/floor, sample rates, latency, displayed numerical tolerances, silence/nonfinite handling, persistence, automation availability, undo/redo, cancellation, malformed state, engine/device failure and teardown have no target outcomes here.
